name: Dog
description: The body a player is, in the dog game: Kimi's Bernese mountain dog in harness and saddlebag, one faceted low-poly shell of 12,229 triangles generated with the Tripo API from the concept painting, rigged in game-architect-studio with 25 bones (spine, neck, head, jaw, two hanging ears, a three-bone tail, fore legs of scapula, upper arm, forearm and paw, hind legs of thigh, shin and paw) and carrying the clips a dog needs before any object speaks. The four gaits were authored on an IK control layer with each paw planted on the ground and baked onto the bones, so a foot in a stance does not slide; the speed each gait was authored for comes out of that geometry and is stated per clip.

sockets.name: mouth
sockets.description: Under the nose, at the tip of the jaw. The one thing movement.carry_in_mouth holds rides here, so it follows the jaw through a sniff, a bark and a drag. Parented to the jaw bone.

sockets.name: collar
sockets.description: The front of the neck, where the painted collar sits and a leash clips. Parented to the neck bone.

sockets.name: back
sockets.description: The top of the back at the saddlebag's handle, where a blanket or a pack is carried. Parented to the spine bone.

sockets.name: head_top
sockets.description: Crown of the head, between the ears. Parented to the head bone.

animations.name: idle
animations.description: A breath, a slow wag, one ear flick, a glance left and back.

animations.name: walk
animations.description: Four-beat lateral sequence: hind left, fore left, hind right, fore right, a quarter apart. Each paw planted for a 0.36 m stance: authored for 0.774 m/s.

animations.name: trot
animations.description: Diagonal pairs half a cycle apart, paws planted for a 0.40 m stance: authored for 1.92 m/s.

animations.name: run
animations.description: Rotary gallop: the hind pair close together, then the fore pair, the back bunching and stretching under them. Paws planted for a 0.50 m stance: authored for 3.0 m/s.

animations.name: drag
animations.description: A walk with the weight back and the head low: the mouth is on something heavier than the dog lifts. Paws planted for a 0.28 m stance: authored for 0.4 m/s. movement.carry_in_mouth's dragSpeedFactor is why it is slow.

animations.name: sniff
animations.description: Nose down: the chest pitches, the neck and head drop, the nose sweeps, the fore legs bend. The mouth socket comes down to about 0.2 m.

animations.name: sniff_air
animations.description: Nose up, on the wind: the head lifts, the mouth socket to 0.93 m, and casts slowly.

animations.name: dig
animations.description: The fore paws scrape alternately with the elbows bent, the chest low, the rump up, the head down watching the hole, the tail up. One cycle is one scrape of each paw; housing.den_and_cache counts the seconds.

animations.name: sit
animations.description: Down onto the haunches over half a second, then held: hind legs folded, rump dropped, back sloping up to square shoulders.

animations.name: lie
animations.description: The sphinx over a second: fore legs out in front, hind legs folded under, the chest down to the ground, head up then lowered toward the paws. What housing.den_and_cache's rest looks like.

animations.name: bark
animations.description: Head back, jaw open 34 degrees, chest up, a hop of the fore paws; then shut. The brick drops what the mouth holds on a bark, so the open jaw is also what the player sees.

animations.name: mark
animations.description: The right hind leg lifts out and up, holds, and comes down; the weight shifts left to carry it.

source.tool: Tripo API (body) and blender-mcp-asset-pipeline 1.0.3 on Blender 4.4.3 (rig, clips, export)
source.sourceFile: Riverside Bernese Dog.glb, 27458020 bytes, sha256 5b736b3e0ac7daedb9c91812218608c70568406b4f491ebd097f0980ccfb18dd, from Kimi's 'Kimi_Agent_Dog Survival Game Pitch.zip' (9 Nov 2026); not in either repository, named by hash in the script

provenance: The yard (game-architect-studio #150) drew its dog as nine boxes turned as one, which is an honest grey-box and cannot sit, dig or put its nose down. Three rigged bodies followed in the studio's build script: the boxes rigged as they stood, a voxel-remeshed shell of them, and a lofted low-poly tube body with a vertex-colour palette; each read wrong beside the concept painting of a faceted Bernese in harness and saddlebag, and Alexander said so. On 9 Nov 2026 Kimi generated that painting's dog with the Tripo API ('Riverside Bernese Dog', one shell of 12,229 triangles, 4K coat with normal and roughness maps, Y-up metres, no rig) and shipped it in the pitch zip; rights to Tripo output rest with the generating account under Tripo's terms, to be confirmed against the plan tier before the game is published. The studio's script takes that file by sha256 and makes the asset from it: welded (Tripo writes every facet with its own vertices, 16,922 of them with every edge a boundary, which no automatic weighting can cross), flat-shaded, the coat resampled to 1K and written as JPEG, the normal and roughness maps dropped as a flat-shaded low-poly body has no use for them, bones placed on measured centrelines of the shell, automatic weights with the 289 vertices of the loose harness and bag parts assigned to their nearest bone. The rig follows what P2Design's course squirrel teaches: deform bones the mesh follows, and a control layer of IK paw targets and poles that the gaits are keyed on and that is baked onto the bones and deleted before export, so the four gaits have planted feet (the stance length and time of each is what its authored speed is) while the poses stay forward-kinematic. Clips are named for a pack's bricks: sniff and sniff_air for world.scent_field's two nose modes, drag for movement.carry_in_mouth's heavy things, dig and lie for housing.den_and_cache, bark and mark for the two inputs that lay or drop scent. Every pose axis is pinned and checked on the evaluated rig before export; an asset whose walk went backwards would otherwise pass every file-level check there is.
